subject: tourism
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 (with one optional module) · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: very short answers 2 marks (30–50 words), short answers 3 marks (50–80 words), long answers 6 marks (80–120 words).
Section C: attempt either Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business) or Optional Module II (Hospitality Management) in all its questions.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why do governments of tourist-sending countries issue travel advisories?
questions.answer: Where there is political instability, conflict or terrorism, law and order is weak and tourists are unsafe. The advisory warns their citizens not to go, or to leave at once.

questions.q: Describe any two features of a tourist map.
questions.answer: It shows places of tourist interest such as scenic spots, hill stations, monuments, religious places, beaches and sanctuaries. It also shows their location in relation to rivers, lakes, mountains and forests and is prepared from national to local level.

questions.q: Give two characteristics of road transport.
questions.answer: It is flexible, reliable and cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. Vehicles such as cars, buses, taxis and jeeps connect rail, air and water transport.

questions.q: Mention the incident about Tansen recorded in the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri.
questions.answer: It records that the Sufi Shaikh Salim Chishti of Fatehpur Sikri, at the time of his death, expressed the last wish to hear Tansen sing. Jahangir calls Tansen 'unequalled as a singer'.

questions.q: Describe the town planning of the Harappan cities in two points.
questions.answer: Cities were built on a grid pattern with roads that cut each other at right angles. They had a citadel on high ground, an advanced drainage system and houses of well-baked bricks.

questions.q: Describe the sacred value of Mathura in any two points.
questions.answer: Mathura is the birthplace of Lord Krishna on the Yamuna and is known as Brajbhoomi. Holi and Janmashtami draw pilgrims and tourists to Mathura and Vrindavan.

questions.q: How did Christianity come to India? Explain in two points.
questions.answer: St Thomas, a disciple of Jesus, is believed to have reached Muziris on the western coast and founded churches. The Portuguese later brought missionaries such as Francis Xavier to the western coast.

questions.q: Differentiate between a domestic and an international tourist.
questions.answer: A domestic tourist travels within his own country and stays at least 24 hours away from home. An international tourist visits another country on a foreign passport and stays at least 24 hours without a paid job.

questions.q: Elucidate the four stages of team development.
questions.answer: Forming: members are cautious and explore. Storming: conflict about goals and roles surfaces. Norming: members agree on decision-making and standards. Performing: the team works together to get results.

questions.q: What is the marketing mix?
questions.answer: It is the set of controllable tools a firm blends to get the response it wants: product, price, promotion and place, with people, physical evidence and process added for services.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the main features of Islamic culture (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Islam is monotheistic and its five pillars are faith, prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj. (ii) Muslims pray five times a day facing Mecca. (iii) Sufis preached peace and brotherhood and their dargahs and Urs attract all communities.

questions.q: Describe the pattern of foreign tourist arrivals in India (three points).
questions.answer: (i) In 2014 the USA (14.57%), Bangladesh (12.27%) and the UK (10.92%) were the top source countries. (ii) The top ten countries gave about 61.5% of the arrivals. (iii) Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi received most foreign tourists and tourists stay a little over a month.

questions.q: Explain the share of the world regions in international tourist arrivals in 2015 (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Europe had the highest share, 609 million (51%). (ii) Asia and the Pacific followed with 278 million (23%), then the Americas with 191 million. (iii) Africa had the minimum, 53 million (5%), and the Middle East 54 million.

questions.q: How should a tourism professional handle customer complaints? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Listen sympathetically, stay calm and do not take it personally. (ii) Record the details and deal with written complaints at once. (iii) Offer repair, replacement or refund, follow up and report back with a solution.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the major Jain heritage sites of India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Mount Parsvanatha in Bihar, where twenty Tirthankaras attained moksha. (ii) Pawapuri, where Mahavira attained nirvana. (iii) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu in white marble. (iv) Ranakpur with 1,444 carved pillars. (v) Girnar and Shatrunjaya in Gujarat. (vi) Shravanabelagola with the 57-ft Bahubali statue.

questions.q: Describe five important Christian heritage sites in India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa), with St Francis Xavier's relics. (ii) St Thomas Mount and San Thomas Basilica in Chennai. (iii) Velankanni church in Tamil Nadu. (iv) Thomas Church at Kodungallur in Kerala. (v) Skinner's church in Delhi, the Holy Christ Church in Shimla and the Sardhana church. (vi) The Presbyterian church at Ross Island and Solomon's Temple at Aizawl.

sections.title: Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between a retail travel agency and a wholesale travel agency with an example.
questions.answer: (i) A retail agency sells packages directly to tourists and earns commission; a wholesale agency buys in bulk and does not sell directly. (ii) A retail agency works on commission and mark-up; a wholesale agency earns through discounts on bulk reservations. (iii) For example, a local agency booking a Goa trip is a retailer while a firm that blocks hotel rooms and flight seats to make packages is a wholesaler.

questions.q: Explain the importance of disaster preparedness for travel agencies (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Safety and security of visitors is the prime responsibility. (ii) Disasters such as floods, earthquakes and terror strikes are uncertain. (iii) Trained teams coordinate with local disaster management teams to prevent harm.

sections.title: Optional Module II (Hospitality Management): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three expectations of guests during their arrival at the hotel.
questions.answer: (i) A warm and friendly greeting and welcome. (ii) An efficient and quick check-in with clean, well-maintained rooms. (iii) Efficient luggage handling by the bell desk from car to room.

questions.q: Explain the steps in handling a fire emergency in a hotel (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Inform the fire-fighting department with exact location and size of the fire. (ii) Alert all guests to use the staircase, not the lift, and help the old and handicapped. (iii) Assemble outside for roll call and use extinguishers.
